item.description:

Why: Studies Van Hove singularities in superconductivity, directly relevant to kagome physics and unconventional SC.

Abstract: Using determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations, the authors compute here the superconducting transition temperature T c of the two-dimensional attractive Hubbard model near ordinary and higher-order Van Hove singularities. Abstract: Here, the authors show how strain allows control of the spatiotemporal exciton dynamics in WSe 2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures. They demonstrate that tensile strain abruptly increases the excess energy of hot excitons, thereby accelerating their transient diffusion. The authors trace this back to suppressed phonon-mediated scattering from bright to dark excitons. Furthermore, a periodic modulation of the transient exciton diffusion is predicted in the presence of a compressive strain resulting from emission of M phonons.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Emergent Mott insulating phase at cuprate interfaces, relevant to correlated electronic structure.

Tags: #cuprate #heterostructure #Mottinsulator

Abstract: The p - n junction is at the heart of the first great technological revolution. Here, the authors fabricate and characterize such a junction made entirely out of cuprates superconductors thin films. They observe a charge transfer between n -type Pr 1 . 85 Ce 0 . 15 CuO 4 and p -type La 1 . 85 Sr 0 . 15 CuO 4 , from which a Mott insulating layer emerges at the atomically sharp interface. They first assess the quality of the structure through x-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy and then they explore the nature of the insulating interface arising from strong electron correlations with various electrical transport experiments.
